{{< include /_disclaimer.qmd >}}

# Scope

**Sentence Reading Efficiency (SRE)** is a speeded literacy measure adapted
from ROAR ([intro-sre](https://roar.stanford.edu/technical/intro-sre.html);
Yeatman et al., 2024). Children read simple sentences one at a time and judge
each *true* or *false* (2AFC), reading as many as they can in **180 seconds**.
ROAR's official score is **correct − incorrect** within the time window — the
subtraction is a guessing correction (a random guesser nets ≈ 0). LEVANTE
originally z-scored this count within dataset so it sits on a roughly
comparable scale to the IRT tasks
(`score_type = "guessing_adjusted_number_correct_scaled"`).

**The scoring bug, and its fix.** The original `levantemodels::score_sre()`
computed `filter(trial_number <= 180)` then
`(sum(correct) - sum(!correct)) / 180`, i.e. it truncated at the first 180
**trials**, not 180 **seconds**. (The `/180` divisor is cosmetic: it cancels
in the z-score.) This chapter's July 2026 analysis proposed scoring a rate
instead, and production has since adopted one (section 2). This notebook
asks:

1. **Timing forensics**: do runs actually last 180 seconds? (Spoiler: no;
   there is real structure here, including double-length runs.)
2. **Rate scoring**: how much do scores change from the legacy rule to the
   production rate? Do correlations with age, ROAR-Phoneme (PA) and
   ROAR-Word (SWR), and stability across waves, change?
3. **Efficiency scoring**: correctness + RT models (drift-diffusion IRT and
   alternatives), with a zero-filled IRT model, EZ-diffusion and a
   hierarchical speed–accuracy model fit to the trial data.

Data: `levante_data_latest` v3_17 (pinned for this study and loaded with
`load_levante_latest()`; the exact reference is printed with the first
table), all datasets with SRE data: SRE
trials, run metadata (age, start time) and the production scores,
including the PA/SWR/Vocab/TROG θ used as validity criteria. Only runs that
production scored without an exclusion have trials, so the analysis is on
valid runs.

::: {.callout-note}
## 2026-10-30: moved to `levante_data_latest` v3_17
This chapter was first written in July 2026 on the hackathon dataset and
then moved to the model calibration dataset. It now runs on the pinned
release, which adds Argentina, the UK and Ghana, and second waves for
Germany and rural Colombia. Other changes in this revision:

- Production now scores SRE as a rate, so section 2 compares the legacy rule
  with the production rate.
- **The validity criteria now take each child's first run *per task*.**
  Before this fix, one run per child was kept across PA/SWR (and across
  PA/SWR/Vocab/TROG in the scoreboard), so each child counted toward only
  the criterion they happened to do first. That error had made the SA
  composite look more valid than the rate on Vocab.
- Zero-fill and the SA model are refit on v3_17. The diffusion-IRT model is
  not, and its section is marked stale.
- Germany's 3.6-month retest (a separate v1_2 pull of 23 pairs) is replaced
  by stability across waves within v3_17.

Every number in the text is computed from the data when the chapter renders.
:::

```{r setup}
source(here::here("common.R"))

# levante_data_latest, pinned in common.R. Only runs that production scored
# without an exclusion have trials, so the trial data are the valid runs.
scores_latest <- load_levante_latest("scores", version = "v3_17")
trials_latest <- load_levante_latest("trials", version = "v3_17")
data_ref <- unique(trials_latest$redivis_source)

# run metadata and the validity criteria (production PA/SWR/Vocab/TROG θ),
# in the shapes the code below uses
run_data <- scores_latest |> distinct(run_id, user_id, age, time_started)
participants <- scores_latest |> distinct(user_id, dataset)
registry_scores <- scores_latest |>
  filter(task_id %in% c("pa", "swr", "vocab", "trog"), is.na(exclusion),
         !is.na(score)) |>
  select(task = task_id, run_id, ability = score)

sre <- trials_latest |>
  filter(task_id == "sre") |>
  mutate(rt_s = rt_numeric / 1000,
         corpus = sub("_[0-9]+$", "", item_uid) |> str_remove("^sre_"))

# datasets in order of SRE runs
sre_datasets <- sre |> count(dataset, sort = TRUE) |> pull(dataset)
dataset_pal <- set_names(
  RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(max(3, length(sre_datasets)), "Set1")[seq_along(sre_datasets)],
  dataset_labels_named[sre_datasets])

label_dataset <- \(df) df |>
  mutate(dataset_label = factor(dataset_labels_named[dataset],
                                levels = names(dataset_pal)))

sre <- label_dataset(sre)

# for the prose: r to two decimals without the leading zero, a fail-loud
# one-value lookup, and a dataset's label from its code
f2 <- \(x) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf("%.2f", x))
pick <- function(df, col, ...) {
  x <- dplyr::filter(df, ...) |> dplyr::pull({{ col }})
  if (length(x) != 1) stop("pick(): expected 1 row, got ", length(x))
  x
}
dl <- \(d) dataset_labels_named[[d]]
# one validity r from a table with dataset_label and criterion columns
vr <- \(tab, col, d, crit) f2(pick(tab, {{ col }}, dataset_label == dl(d),
                                   criterion == crit))

# the production SRE score (a rate; see section 2) plus run metadata
sre_scores_pub <- scores_latest |>
  filter(task_id == "sre", run_id %in% sre$run_id) |>
  select(dataset, run_id, user_id, age, time_started, score_prod = score) |>
  label_dataset()
```

```{r data-counts}
sre |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(runs = n_distinct(run_id), children = n_distinct(user_id),
            trials = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = glue("SRE trial data by dataset (`{data_ref}`)"))
```

# 1. Timing forensics: is 180 seconds always 180 seconds?

Two per-run duration measures: **time-on-sentences** (cumulative RT — the
task records per-sentence RT in ms) and **wall-clock span** (last minus first
trial server timestamp). Neither is exactly the timer, but they bracket it:
cumulative RT omits inter-trial overhead; timestamp span omits the first
trial's duration and can inflate under server lag or pauses.

```{r durations}
run_time <- sre |>
  group_by(dataset, dataset_label, run_id, user_id) |>
  summarise(n_trials = n(),
            n_corpora = n_distinct(corpus),
            cum_rt = sum(rt_s),
            span = as.numeric(difftime(max(timestamp), min(timestamp),
                                       units = "secs")),
            n_correct = sum(correct), n_incorrect = sum(!correct),
            .groups = "drop")

dur_tab <- run_time |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(across(c(cum_rt, span),
                   list(q05 = ~quantile(.x, .05), median = median,
                        q95 = ~quantile(.x, .95), max = max)),
            .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(dur_tab, digits = 0,
               caption = "Per-run duration (seconds): cumulative RT and wall-clock span")
```

```{r duration-hist, fig.height=4}
run_time |>
  ggplot(aes(x = cum_rt, fill = dataset_label)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset_label), scales = "free_y") +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 180, lty = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_pal) +
  labs(x = "Cumulative RT per run (s)", y = "Runs",
       title = "Most runs sum to just under 180 s of reading time",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = nominal 180 s deadline. Note the Canadian runs near 330 s.")
```

Three regularities:

- **The 180 s deadline is real but not exact.** Median time on sentences is
  `r round(min(dur_tab$cum_rt_median))`–`r round(max(dur_tab$cum_rt_median))` s
  by dataset (the rest is inter-trial overhead: wall-clock span medians are
  `r round(min(dur_tab$span_median))`–`r round(max(dur_tab$span_median))` s).
  So the timer fires on schedule for most runs.
- **A left tail of short runs exists everywhere**, heaviest in Argentina
  (5th percentile
  `r round(pick(dur_tab, cum_rt_q05, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")))` s
  of reading time) and rural Colombia
  (`r round(pick(dur_tab, cum_rt_q05, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_rural")))` s).
  The legacy rule scored these short runs as if the child had had the full
  window.
- **Canada (Western) has genuinely double-length runs.**

## Block structure: some Canadian runs contain two 180-s blocks

The item bank prefix identifies sentence corpora. Colombia and Argentina
interleave three corpora (`spanish_lab`, `spanish_ai`, `spanish_ai_human`)
*within one timed block*; Germany uses one corpus (`uzh`); the UK, Ghana and
most Canadian runs use one English corpus per run. But some Canadian runs
contain **two sequential blocks** (`lab` sentences, then `ai` sentences),
each with its own ~180-s window: roughly 360 s of testing scored as if it
were one window.

```{r blocks}
run_blocks <- sre |>
  group_by(dataset_label, run_id, corpus) |>
  summarise(block_rt = sum(rt_s), n = n(), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  summarise(blocks = paste(sort(corpus), collapse = " + "),
            two_windows = sum(block_rt > 120) >= 2,
            .groups = "drop")

run_blocks |>
  count(dataset_label, blocks, two_windows) |>
  arrange(dataset_label, desc(n)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Corpus composition of runs. two_windows = ≥2 corpora each with >120 s of reading time (sequential blocks, not interleaving)")
```

All `r sum(run_blocks$two_windows)` two-window runs are in
`r paste(unique(run_blocks$dataset_label[run_blocks$two_windows]), collapse = ", ")`.
They are early runs (task versions 1.15.x), tagged `es-CO` although their
sentences come from the English corpora.

```{r trials-per-run, fig.height=4}
run_time |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n_trials, fill = dataset_label)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset_label), scales = "free_y") +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, boundary = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 180, lty = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_pal) +
  labs(x = "Trials per run", y = "Runs",
       title = "Only Canada ever reaches the 180-trial truncation point",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = the legacy rule's truncation at 180 trials")
```

**Side-quest verdict:** the legacy first-180-*trials* filter was a no-op
outside Canada (no run elsewhere exceeds 180 trials; the maximum is
`r max(run_time$n_trials[run_time$dataset != "pilot_western_ca_main"])`). It
bit only in Canada (`r sum(run_time$n_trials > 180)` runs exceed 180 trials,
maximum `r max(run_time$n_trials)`), and there it truncated arbitrarily
*across* the two-block structure. Meanwhile the actual problem is the
reverse: **reading time varies from
`r round(quantile(run_time$cum_rt, .05))` s (5th percentile) to
`r round(max(run_time$cum_rt))` s across runs**, and a raw count treats them
all as equal.

# 2. Rate scoring, now in production

Production SRE scoring is now a **rate** (`score_type =
"guessing_adjusted_rate_scaled"` in `r data_ref`): net correct per second
of wall-clock span (first to last trial timestamp), z-scored within dataset,
with runs shorter than 30 s left unscored,

$$\text{score} = z\!\left(\frac{C - I}{\text{span (s)}}\right).$$

This is the fix this chapter originally proposed, except for the
denominator: the proposal divided by cumulative RT (time on sentences), and
production divides by wall-clock span. The two agree closely (sensitivity
check below). The legacy rule (the first 180 *trials*, C − I, z-scored
within dataset) is recomputed from the trials as the comparison score.

First, check that the production score can be reproduced from the trials:

```{r replicate-published}
min_time <- 30

prod_check <- run_time |>
  filter(span >= min_time) |>
  mutate(rate_span = (n_correct - n_incorrect) / span) |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  mutate(z = scale(rate_span)[, 1]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  inner_join(sre_scores_pub |> select(run_id, score_prod), by = "run_id") |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(n = n(), r = cor(z, score_prod),
            max_abs_diff = max(abs(z - score_prod)), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(prod_check, digits = 3,
             caption = "Production SRE score vs a reimplementation from the trials")

# the legacy rule: first 180 trials, (C − I) z-scored within dataset
old_score <- sre |>
  group_by(dataset, run_id) |>
  filter(trial_number <= 180) |>
  summarise(net = sum(correct) - sum(!correct), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  mutate(score_old = scale(net)[, 1]) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r corrected-score}
# score_new is the production rate score; `rate` is net correct per 180 s
new_score <- run_time |>
  inner_join(sre_scores_pub |> select(run_id, score_new = score_prod),
             by = "run_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(score_new)) |>
  mutate(rate = (n_correct - n_incorrect) / span * 180)

scores_cmp <- new_score |>
  inner_join(old_score |> select(dataset, run_id, net, score_old),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  left_join(sre_scores_pub |> select(dataset, run_id, age),
            by = c("dataset", "run_id"))
```

The reimplementation matches production to rounding (r rounds to
`r sprintf("%.3f", min(prod_check$r))` in every dataset, and the largest
difference is `r sprintf("%.3f", max(prod_check$max_abs_diff))` z). Left
unscored by the 30-s floor: `r nrow(run_time) - nrow(new_score)` runs.

## A) How much do scores change?

```{r old-vs-new, fig.height=4.5}
cors <- scores_cmp |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(n = n(), r = cor(score_old, score_new),
            r_spearman = cor(score_old, score_new, method = "spearman"),
            mean_abs_change = mean(abs(score_new - score_old)),
            max_abs_change = max(abs(score_new - score_old)),
            .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(cors, digits = 2,
             caption = "Legacy (first 180 trials) vs production rate z-scores")

scores_cmp |>
  ggplot(aes(x = score_old, y = score_new, color = dataset_label)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset_label)) +
  geom_abline(lty = 3, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_pal) +
  labs(x = "Legacy score (z)", y = "Rate score (z)",
       title = "Legacy vs rate SRE scores")
```

```{r movers}
scores_cmp |>
  mutate(change = score_new - score_old) |>
  slice_max(abs(change), n = 10) |>
  select(dataset_label, n_trials, span, n_correct, n_incorrect,
         score_old, score_new, change) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Largest score changes from the legacy rule to the rate")
```

```{r change-vs-time, fig.height=4}
scores_cmp |>
  mutate(change = score_new - score_old) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = span, y = change, color = dataset_label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lty = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 180, lty = 2, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Wall-clock span per run (s)", y = "Rate − legacy (z)",
       title = "Who moves: short runs move up, double-length runs move down") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## B) Validity correlations, legacy vs rate

Within each dataset: correlations of SRE with age, ROAR-Phoneme (θ), and
ROAR-Word (θ). Cross-run joins take each child's first run per task (fixed
2026-10-30; see the note at the top).

```{r validity}
first_run <- \(df, ...) df |>
  group_by(dataset, user_id, ...) |>
  arrange(time_started) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup()

pa_swr <- registry_scores |>
  filter(task %in% c("pa", "swr"), !is.na(ability)) |>
  left_join(run_data |> select(run_id, user_id, time_started), by = "run_id") |>
  left_join(participants |> select(user_id, dataset), by = "user_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(dataset)) |>
  first_run(task) |>
  select(dataset, user_id, task, other = ability) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = task, values_from = other)

sre_first <- sre_scores_pub |>
  first_run() |>
  select(dataset, dataset_label, user_id, run_id, age) |>
  inner_join(scores_cmp |> select(dataset, run_id, score_old, score_new),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  left_join(pa_swr, by = c("dataset", "user_id"))

validity_b <- sre_first |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(dataset_label, criterion) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_legacy = cor(score_old, crit),
            r_rate = cor(score_new, crit), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(delta = r_rate - r_legacy)

knitr::kable(validity_b, digits = 2,
             caption = "SRE validity correlations within dataset, legacy vs rate scoring")
```

```{r validity-pooled}
pooled <- sre_first |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(criterion) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_legacy = cor(score_old, crit),
            r_rate = cor(score_new, crit), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(delta = r_rate - r_legacy)

knitr::kable(pooled, digits = 2,
             caption = "Pooled across datasets (all scores z-scaled within dataset; PA/SWR θ are by-language, so pooled r mixes calibrations — interpret within-site values first)")
```

The rate is about as valid as the legacy score in most datasets. It is
clearly more valid in Canada (SWR
`r vr(validity_b, r_legacy, "pilot_western_ca_main", "swr")` →
`r vr(validity_b, r_rate, "pilot_western_ca_main", "swr")`), where the
double-block runs no longer count double, and less valid in Argentina (SWR
`r vr(validity_b, r_legacy, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "swr")` →
`r vr(validity_b, r_rate, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "swr")`). The cause in
Argentina is short runs. The rate extrapolates a short run's few responses
to a full window, while the legacy count stays low, and Argentina has far
more short runs than anywhere else:

```{r short-runs}
short_cut <- 120

first_span <- sre_first |>
  inner_join(scores_cmp |> select(run_id, span), by = "run_id")

short_share <- first_span |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(n = n(), share_short = mean(span < short_cut),
            age_short = mean(age[span < short_cut], na.rm = TRUE),
            age_other = mean(age[span >= short_cut], na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(short_share, digits = 2,
             caption = glue("Share of children's first runs shorter than {short_cut} s of wall-clock time, and mean age of children with short and other runs"))

validity_long <- first_span |>
  filter(span >= short_cut) |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(dataset_label, criterion) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_legacy = cor(score_old, crit),
            r_rate = cor(score_new, crit), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(delta = r_rate - r_legacy)

validity_b |>
  select(dataset_label, criterion, delta_all = delta) |>
  inner_join(validity_long |> select(dataset_label, criterion, delta_long = delta),
             by = c("dataset_label", "criterion")) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = glue("Rate − legacy validity, all first runs vs first runs of at least {short_cut} s"))
```

`r round(100 * pick(short_share, share_short, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")))`%
of Argentine children's first runs are shorter than `r short_cut` s, against
at most
`r round(100 * max(short_share$share_short[short_share$dataset_label != dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")]))`%
elsewhere. Among runs of at least `r short_cut` s the two scores are equally
valid in Argentina (SWR
`r vr(validity_long, r_legacy, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "swr")` vs
`r vr(validity_long, r_rate, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "swr")`). The children
with short runs are younger on average
(`r round(pick(short_share, age_short, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")), 1)`
vs
`r round(pick(short_share, age_other, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")), 1)`
years). What ends these runs early isn't determined here.

## Stability across waves

The table covers datasets with at least 20 children whose first two SRE
runs are six months or more apart. Rank-order stability across that gap is a
demanding criterion: a better score should preserve more true-score
variance.

```{r stability}
# Rank-order stability per dataset: each child's first two runs, kept if at
# least stab_min_gap days apart; datasets with >= 20 such pairs. Runs missing
# any of `cols` are dropped first, so every score is compared on the same pairs.
stab_min_gap <- 180

stability_by_dataset <- function(run_scores, cols) {
  run_scores |>
    select(dataset, run_id, all_of(cols)) |>
    drop_na() |>
    inner_join(sre_scores_pub |> select(run_id, user_id, time_started),
               by = "run_id") |>
    pivot_longer(all_of(cols), names_to = "score") |>
    group_by(dataset, score, user_id) |>
    arrange(time_started, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    filter(n() >= 2) |>
    summarise(gap = as.numeric(difftime(time_started[2], time_started[1],
                                        units = "days")),
              t1 = value[1], t2 = value[2], .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(gap >= stab_min_gap) |>
    group_by(dataset, score) |>
    filter(n() >= 20) |>
    summarise(n_pairs = n(), gap_months = median(gap) / 30.4,
              r = cor(t1, t2), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = score, values_from = r) |>
    label_dataset() |>
    arrange(dataset_label) |>
    select(dataset_label, n_pairs, gap_months, all_of(cols))
}

stab_tab <- stability_by_dataset(scores_cmp, c("score_old", "score_new"))

knitr::kable(stab_tab, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Dataset", "Pairs", "Median gap (months)",
                           "Legacy", "Rate"),
             caption = "Rank-order stability across waves, legacy vs rate")
```

The two scores are equally stable: they differ by at most
`r f2(max(abs(stab_tab$score_new - stab_tab$score_old)))` in any dataset.

## Sensitivity: denominator choice

```{r denominator-sensitivity}
sens <- run_time |>
  filter(cum_rt >= min_time, span >= min_time) |>
  mutate(rate_rt = (n_correct - n_incorrect) / cum_rt * 180,
         rate_span = (n_correct - n_incorrect) / span * 180) |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(n = n(), r_rt_vs_span = cor(rate_rt, rate_span), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(sens, digits = 3,
             caption = "Rate via cumulative RT vs via wall-clock span")
```

Dividing by cumulative RT or by wall-clock span gives nearly the same rate
(r ≥ `r f2(min(sens$r_rt_vs_span))` in every dataset), so production's
choice of span over this chapter's cumulative RT makes little difference.

# 3. Fast guessing: the bridge to model-based scoring

The `C − I` correction neutralizes guessing *in expectation* (a guesser nets
≈ 0), but guessing still costs signal: guessed trials burn testing time and
add noise. And guessing is far from uniform across sites:

```{r fast-guessing, fig.height=4}
sre |>
  mutate(rt_bin = cut(rt_s, c(0, .5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, Inf))) |>
  group_by(dataset_label, rt_bin) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct), pct = n(), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  mutate(pct = pct / sum(pct)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = rt_bin, y = accuracy, color = dataset_label,
             group = dataset_label)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, lty = 3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(size = pct), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "RT (s)", y = "Accuracy",
       title = "Sub-second responses are mostly at chance, and how common they are varies hugely by site",
       subtitle = "Point size ∝ share of site's trials in that RT bin; dotted line = 2AFC chance") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r guessing-table}
guess_tab <- sre |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(pct_rt_under_1s = mean(rt_s < 1),
            acc_under_1s = mean(correct[rt_s < 1]),
            acc_over_1s = mean(correct[rt_s >= 1]), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(guess_tab, digits = 2, caption = "Fast-guessing prevalence by dataset")
```

Sub-second responses range from
`r round(100 * min(guess_tab$pct_rt_under_1s))`% of trials
(`r guess_tab$dataset_label[which.min(guess_tab$pct_rt_under_1s)]`) to
`r round(100 * max(guess_tab$pct_rt_under_1s))`%
(`r guess_tab$dataset_label[which.max(guess_tab$pct_rt_under_1s)]`). In the
Spanish-speaking sites and Ghana they are at chance, i.e. guesses. In the UK,
Canada and Germany they are mostly correct
(`r f2(pick(guess_tab, acc_under_1s, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_sheffield_gb_main")))`,
`r f2(pick(guess_tab, acc_under_1s, dataset_label == dl("pilot_western_ca_main")))`
and
`r f2(pick(guess_tab, acc_under_1s, dataset_label == dl("pilot_mpieva_de_main")))`),
so there they come from genuinely fast readers.

**Ghana is different.** Accuracy is near chance even on responses slower
than 1 s
(`r f2(pick(guess_tab, acc_over_1s, dataset_label == dl("pilot_capecoast_gh_main")))`),
so few children there were reading the sentences successfully, and the
rate score is unrelated to age (r =
`r vr(validity_b, r_rate, "pilot_capecoast_gh_main", "age")`, n =
`r pick(validity_b, n, dataset_label == dl("pilot_capecoast_gh_main"), criterion == "age")`).
Ghana's SRE scores carry little information as things stand.

This is a strong argument for scoring models that use the joint
(correct, RT) signal per trial, rather than counts alone.

# 4. Toward an efficiency score from correctness + RT

## The modeling landscape

SRE's design — self-paced 2AFC trials under a global deadline, with
per-trial RT and accuracy — admits several principled treatments:

1. **Rate normalization (now in production).** Minimal fix: net correct per
   unit time. Already a speed–accuracy composite; requires no model. Its
   weakness: it treats a slow-and-accurate child and a fast-and-sloppy child
   with equal net rates as identical, and fast guessing adds noise it can
   only average over.

2. **Count models (Rasch Poisson counts / offset-Poisson GLMM).** The
   classical psychometrics of speed tests (Rasch, 1960): model the *count* of
   correct responses with a log link and `offset(log(time))`, giving each
   child a latent log-rate; corpus/site enter as fixed effects, children as
   random effects. This is rate normalization done as a measurement model —
   it handles varying time windows natively and yields standard errors. It
   still ignores per-trial RT structure.

3. **Diffusion IRT (van der Maas et al., 2011; Molenaar et al., 2015;
   `diffIRT`, or GLMM approximations).** Each trial's (choice, RT) is a
   Wiener first-passage process; person drift rate $v$ *is* reading
   efficiency, boundary separation $a$ is caution, $T_{er}$ is encoding/motor
   time. Items get drift/boundary loadings. This cleanly separates ability
   from speed–accuracy tradeoff and soaks up fast guesses (they are
   low-drift/low-boundary behavior, not ability). Cost: heavy estimation,
   and item-level calibration needs enough responses per item.

4. **Hierarchical speed–accuracy models (van der Linden, 2007).** Separate
   IRT model for accuracy and lognormal model for RT, with correlated person
   ability θ and speed τ. Less mechanistic than the diffusion model; scales
   well; efficiency is a composite of θ and τ.

5. **Signed residual time scoring (Maris & van der Maas, 2012).** Score
   $(2x - 1)(d - t)$ per item — correct-and-fast is best, wrong-and-fast is
   worst. Elegant and provably optimal under a specific IRT model, but it
   assumes a *per-item* deadline $d$; SRE has only a global deadline, so $d$
   would be an arbitrary pseudo-deadline. Not a natural fit.

## Zero-filled IRT (ROAR-team suggestion)

The ROAR team has begun exploring a simple item-based approach: **fill the
response matrix with zeros for unreached items, then fit a standard IRT
model**. Speed enters the score through the block of zeros — a fast accurate
reader clears more of the bank. We fit one dense Rasch model per item bank
(Spanish: Colombia and Argentina jointly; German; English: Canada, the UK
and Ghana; [`_fit_sre_zerofill_irt.R`](\_fit_sre_zerofill_irt.R)).

```{r zerofill}
zf <- read_rds(here("data/sre_zerofill_scores.rds")) |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  mutate(zf_z = scale(theta_zerofill)[, 1]) |>
  ungroup()

zf_first <- sre_first |>
  inner_join(zf |> select(dataset, run_id, zf_z), by = c("dataset", "run_id"))

# bank sizes, and agreement with the rate score
zf_banks <- sre |>
  inner_join(zf |> select(run_id, bank), by = "run_id") |>
  group_by(bank) |>
  summarise(runs = n_distinct(run_id), items = n_distinct(item_uid))
zf_rate_r <- zf |>
  inner_join(scores_cmp |> select(run_id, score_new), by = "run_id") |>
  label_dataset() |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(r = cor(zf_z, score_new))

zf_valid <- zf_first |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(dataset_label, criterion) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_rate = cor(score_new, crit),
            r_zerofill = cor(zf_z, crit), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(zf_valid, digits = 2,
             caption = "Zero-filled Rasch vs rate score: validity")
```

The banks are `r pick(zf_banks, runs, bank == "es")` runs ×
`r pick(zf_banks, items, bank == "es")` items (Spanish),
`r pick(zf_banks, runs, bank == "de")` ×
`r pick(zf_banks, items, bank == "de")` (German) and
`r pick(zf_banks, runs, bank == "en")` ×
`r pick(zf_banks, items, bank == "en")` (English).

```{r zerofill-stability}
zf_stab <- scores_cmp |>
  select(dataset, run_id, score_new) |>
  inner_join(zf |> select(dataset, run_id, zf_z), by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  stability_by_dataset(c("score_new", "zf_z"))

knitr::kable(zf_stab, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Dataset", "Pairs", "Median gap (months)", "Rate",
                           "Zero-fill"),
             caption = "Stability across waves: zero-filled Rasch vs rate")
```

```{r zerofill-guessing}
guess_share <- sre |>
  group_by(dataset, run_id) |>
  summarise(pct_fast = mean(rt_s < 1), .groups = "drop")

zf_guess <- zf_first |>
  inner_join(guess_share, by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_rate_fastguess = cor(score_new, pct_fast),
            r_zerofill_fastguess = cor(zf_z, pct_fast), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(zf_guess, digits = 2,
               caption = "Correlation of each score with a run's fast-guess share (RT < 1 s). Positive = the score REWARDS guessing")
```

Where behavior is clean, zero-fill is close to the rate score by another
route: r =
`r f2(pick(zf_rate_r, r, dataset_label == dl("pilot_mpieva_de_main")))` with
the rate in Germany, similar validity there, and similar stability across
waves in Germany
(`r f2(pick(zf_stab, zf_z, dataset_label == dl("pilot_mpieva_de_main")))` vs
`r f2(pick(zf_stab, score_new, dataset_label == dl("pilot_mpieva_de_main")))`
for the rate) and Bogotá
(`r f2(pick(zf_stab, zf_z, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota")))`
vs
`r f2(pick(zf_stab, score_new, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota")))`).
But it has **no guessing correction**: a fast guesser converts wasted
trials into lucky 1s among the zeros. So where guessing is common, the
zero-fill score is unrelated to a run's fast-guess share (r =
`r f2(pick(zf_guess, r_zerofill_fastguess, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")))`
in Argentina,
`r f2(pick(zf_guess, r_zerofill_fastguess, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_rural")))`
in rural Colombia) while the rate score is clearly lower for guessers
(`r f2(pick(zf_guess, r_rate_fastguess, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")))`,
`r f2(pick(zf_guess, r_rate_fastguess, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_rural")))`).
Zero-fill's validity collapses exactly there (Argentina PA r =
`r vr(zf_valid, r_zerofill, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "pa")` vs
`r vr(zf_valid, r_rate, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "pa")` for the rate; rural
Colombia SWR
`r vr(zf_valid, r_zerofill, "pilot_uniandes_co_rural", "swr")` vs
`r vr(zf_valid, r_rate, "pilot_uniandes_co_rural", "swr")`), and so does its
stability in rural Colombia
(`r f2(pick(zf_stab, zf_z, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_rural")))`
vs
`r f2(pick(zf_stab, score_new, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_rural")))`).

The obvious repair, a fixed 2AFC guessing floor (Rasch with g = .5, as in
the LEVANTE multiple-choice models), **backfired** in the July 2026 analysis
on the earlier data (not re-run here): unreached items are *structural*
zeros, and whole-bank accuracy (~10% for a typical run) sits far below any
g = .5 floor, so the model cannot represent the data (EM failed to converge,
and validity collapsed everywhere, e.g. rural age r = .08).
The floor is right for "attempted and guessed," wrong for "never reached."
A repaired variant would need a different treatment of the two zero types —
at which point the model is no longer the simple suggestion, and the rate
score already does the job.

## Proof of concept: EZ-diffusion per run

The EZ-diffusion model (Wagenmakers, van der Maas, & Grasman, 2007) inverts
the simple diffusion model from three per-person summary statistics
(accuracy, mean and variance of correct RTs) — no item structure, no
iterative fitting. It is the cheapest possible test of whether
diffusion-style decomposition adds validity beyond the rate score.

```{r ez}
ez_diffusion <- function(pc, vrt, mrt, s = 0.1) {
  s2 <- s^2
  L <- qlogis(pc)
  x <- L * (L * pc^2 - L * pc + pc - 0.5) / vrt
  v <- sign(pc - 0.5) * s * x^(1 / 4)
  a <- s2 * L / v
  y <- -v * a / s2
  mdt <- (a / (2 * v)) * (1 - exp(y)) / (1 + exp(y))
  tibble(drift = v, boundary = a, ter = mrt - mdt)
}

ez_run <- sre |>
  filter(rt_s >= 0.25, rt_s <= 30) |>
  group_by(dataset, dataset_label, run_id, user_id) |>
  filter(n() >= 15, sum(correct) >= 10) |>
  summarise(n = n(), pc_raw = mean(correct),
            mrt = mean(rt_s[correct]), vrt = var(rt_s[correct]),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  # edge-correct accuracy away from 0.5 and 1
  mutate(pc = pmin(pmax(pc_raw, 0.5 + 1 / (2 * n)), 1 - 1 / (2 * n)))

ez_run <- bind_cols(ez_run, ez_diffusion(ez_run$pc, ez_run$vrt, ez_run$mrt))

ez_run |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(n_runs = n(), across(c(drift, boundary, ter), median),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median EZ-diffusion parameters by dataset")
```

```{r ez-validity}
ez_first <- sre_first |>
  inner_join(ez_run |> select(dataset, run_id, drift, boundary, ter),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id"))

ez_validity <- ez_first |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(dataset_label, criterion) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_rate = cor(score_new, crit),
            r_drift = cor(drift, crit),
            r_boundary = cor(boundary, crit), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(ez_validity, digits = 2,
             caption = "EZ drift vs rate score: validity correlations")
```

```{r ez-stability}
ez_stab <- scores_cmp |>
  select(dataset, run_id, score_new) |>
  inner_join(ez_run |> select(dataset, run_id, drift),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  stability_by_dataset(c("score_new", "drift"))

knitr::kable(ez_stab, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Dataset", "Pairs", "Median gap (months)", "Rate",
                           "EZ drift"),
             caption = "Stability across waves: rate vs EZ drift")
```

```{r ez-scatter, fig.height=4.5}
ez_first |>
  ggplot(aes(x = score_new, y = drift, color = dataset_label)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset_label), scales = "free_y") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_pal) +
  labs(x = "Corrected rate score (z)", y = "EZ drift rate v",
       title = "EZ drift vs the rate score")
```

## Hierarchical speed–accuracy model (van der Linden 2007 style)

The next rung up from EZ: model accuracy and RT jointly but *separately*,
with crossed run × item random effects (fit by
[`_fit_sre_hierarchical_sa.R`](\_fit_sre_hierarchical_sa.R)):

- accuracy: `correct ~ 0 + dataset + (1|run_id) + (1|item_uid)` (logit GLMM)
  → run-level **ability θ**, with item easiness absorbed by item effects
  (the "IRT part" that EZ lacks);
- speed: `log(rt) ~ 0 + dataset + (1|run_id) + (1|item_uid)` (lognormal LMM)
  → run-level **speed τ** (sign-flipped RT effect), with item
  time-intensities absorbed.

An efficiency composite is z(θ) + z(τ), standardized within dataset.

```{r sa-load}
sa_file <- here("data/sre_sa_estimates.rds")
sa <- read_rds(sa_file)

sa_run <- sa$run |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  mutate(theta_z = scale(theta)[, 1], tau_z = scale(tau)[, 1],
         eff = scale(theta_z + tau_z)[, 1]) |>
  ungroup()

sa_cor <- sa_run |>
  inner_join(scores_cmp |> select(run_id, score_new), by = "run_id") |>
  label_dataset() |>
  group_by(dataset_label) |>
  summarise(n_runs = n(), r_theta_tau = cor(theta, tau),
            r_composite_rate = cor(eff, score_new), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(sa_cor, digits = 2,
             caption = "Ability–speed correlation by dataset (negative where fast responses are mostly guesses), and the SA composite's agreement with the rate score")
```

```{r sa-validity}
sa_first <- sre_first |>
  inner_join(sa_run |> select(dataset, run_id, theta_z, tau_z, eff),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id"))

sa_valid <- sa_first |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(dataset_label, criterion) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_rate = cor(score_new, crit),
            r_theta = cor(theta_z, crit),
            r_tau = cor(tau_z, crit),
            r_composite = cor(eff, crit), .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(sa_valid, digits = 2,
             caption = "Hierarchical SA model vs rate score: validity")
```

```{r sa-stability}
sa_stab <- scores_cmp |>
  select(dataset, run_id, score_new) |>
  inner_join(sa_run |> select(dataset, run_id, theta_z, tau_z, eff),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  stability_by_dataset(c("score_new", "theta_z", "tau_z", "eff"))

knitr::kable(sa_stab, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Dataset", "Pairs", "Median gap (months)", "Rate",
                           "θ", "τ", "Composite"),
             caption = "Stability across waves: SA-model scores vs rate")
```

The decomposition is diagnostic gold but scoring lead. The ability–speed
correlation changes sign across sites, from
`r f2(max(sa_cor$r_theta_tau))`
(`r sa_cor$dataset_label[which.max(sa_cor$r_theta_tau)]`) to
**`r f2(min(sa_cor$r_theta_tau))`**
(`r sa_cor$dataset_label[which.min(sa_cor$r_theta_tau)]`). Where fast
guessing is common, the "speed" dimension is contaminated by disengagement,
so neither τ nor any fixed θ+τ composite travels across sites. The
composite tracks the rate score where behavior is clean (r =
`r f2(pick(sa_cor, r_composite_rate, dataset_label == dl("pilot_mpieva_de_main")))`
in Germany,
`r f2(pick(sa_cor, r_composite_rate, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_sheffield_gb_main")))`
in the UK) and underperforms it where it isn't (Argentina SWR validity
`r vr(sa_valid, r_composite, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "swr")` vs
`r vr(sa_valid, r_rate, "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "swr")`; rural Colombia
stability
`r f2(pick(sa_stab, eff, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_rural")))` vs
`r f2(pick(sa_stab, score_new, dataset_label == dl("pilot_uniandes_co_rural")))`).

## Diffusion IRT (pooled brms Wiener model)

::: {.callout-warning}
## Stale: not re-run on `levante_data_latest`
This model was fit in July 2026 on the retired hackathon dataset
(`levante_data_pilots_hackathon:fpx0:v1_1`; 9.5 h on Sherlock), and it has
not been re-run on `r data_ref`. Its code below is kept for the record but
is not evaluated, and it is left out of the scoreboard. In that fit, after
the 2026-10-30 criterion-join fix, person-level drift was about as valid as
the rate score (slightly higher on SWR, Vocab and TROG) but much less stable
across 16 months in Bogotá (.56 vs .72). Those numbers come from the old
data. Everything else in this chapter is fit on `r data_ref`.
:::

The full model: every trial's (choice, RT) as a Wiener process, with
dataset fixed effects plus run *and item* random effects on drift (the IRT
part), run effects on boundary separation and non-decision time, bias fixed
at .5 (~64k trials; item banks are disjoint across sites, so sites are
linked by priors, not anchors). Prototyped locally with brms
([`_fit_sre_ddm.R`](\_fit_sre_ddm.R)), then exported to raw Stan
([`_export_sre_ddm_stan.R`](\_export_sre_ddm_stan.R)) and fit on Sherlock
([`sherlock_sre_ddm/`](https://github.com/levante-framework/levante-analysis/tree/main/studies/2026-07_sre-scoring/sherlock_sre_ddm); 24 cores, 9.5 h, 4 × 500/500).
Drift-side parameters converged acceptably (R̂ ≤ 1.06); the run-level
non-decision-time hierarchy mixed poorly (R̂ ≈ 1.6) — a known fragility of
ndt under a hard global deadline — which cautions against interpreting the
ndt estimates but leaves the drift comparison intact.

```{r ddm-load}
# fit on the retired hackathon data and not re-run on levante_data_latest;
# the code is kept for the record but not evaluated
ddm_file <- here("data/sre_ddm_estimates.rds")
has_ddm <- FALSE
```

```{r ddm-results, eval=has_ddm}
ddm <- read_rds(ddm_file)

ddm_run <- ddm$run |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  mutate(drift_z = scale(drift_re)[, 1]) |>
  ungroup()

ddm_first <- sre_first |>
  inner_join(ddm_run |> select(dataset, run_id, drift_z, bs_re, ndt_re),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id"))

ddm_first |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(dataset_label, criterion) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            r_rate = cor(score_new, crit),
            r_drift = cor(drift_z, crit),
            r_boundary = cor(bs_re, crit), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = "Diffusion IRT drift vs corrected rate score: validity")
```

```{r ddm-stability, eval=has_ddm}
ddm_stab <- sre_scores_pub |>
  filter(dataset == "pilot_uniandes_co_bogota") |>
  inner_join(ddm_run |> select(dataset, run_id, drift_z),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  inner_join(scores_cmp |> select(dataset, run_id, score_new),
             by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  group_by(user_id) |>
  filter(n() >= 2) |>
  arrange(time_started) |>
  summarise(gap = as.numeric(difftime(time_started[2], time_started[1],
                                      units = "days")),
            across(c(drift_z, score_new), list(t1 = ~.x[1], t2 = ~.x[2])),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(gap > 300)

tibble(n_pairs = nrow(ddm_stab),
       rate = cor(ddm_stab$score_new_t1, ddm_stab$score_new_t2),
       ddm_drift = cor(ddm_stab$drift_z_t1, ddm_stab$drift_z_t2)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = "Bogotá 16-month stability: diffusion-IRT drift vs corrected rate")
```

```{r ddm-corr, eval=has_ddm, fig.height=4.5}
ddm_first |>
  ggplot(aes(x = score_new, y = drift_z, color = dataset_label)) +
  facet_wrap(vars(dataset_label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = dataset_pal) +
  labs(x = "Corrected rate score (z)", y = "DDM-IRT drift (z)",
       title = "Diffusion-IRT drift vs the corrected rate score")
```

In that fit the item side behaved as an IRT model should: item drift
effects tracked empirical item accuracy and (negatively) item RT.

```{r ddm-items, eval=has_ddm, fig.height=4}
item_emp <- sre |>
  group_by(item_uid) |>
  summarise(accuracy = mean(correct), median_rt = median(rt_s), n = n(),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 20)

ddm$item |>
  inner_join(item_emp, by = "item_uid") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = drift_re, y = accuracy)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Item drift effect (logit-ish)", y = "Empirical item accuracy",
       title = "The IRT part works: item drift effects track item difficulty")
```

So the item-level structure that EZ lacked is genuinely recovered here, and
person-level drift was *still* less stable than the rate score.
That localizes the problem: it is not missing item information, it is that
the diffusion decomposition discards stable, valid between-child variance in
*time allocation* (caution, pacing) that the rate score keeps.

# Verdict

**1. The timer is mostly honest, but the legacy trial-count rule was aimed
at the wrong problem.** The first-180-*trials* filter was a no-op outside
Canada and bit only there. The real heterogeneity is in *time*:
`r sum(run_blocks$two_windows)` Canadian runs contain two sequential ~180-s
blocks (~360 s of testing scored as one window), and there is a left tail of
short runs, heaviest in Argentina, that the legacy rule scored as if they
had the full window.

**2. Production now scores SRE as a rate. The switch changes little in
aggregate and a lot for specific children.** Legacy and rate scores
correlate at r ≥
`r f2(min(cors$r[cors$dataset_label != dl("pilot_western_ca_main")]))`
outside Canada but
**`r f2(pick(cors, r, dataset_label == dl("pilot_western_ca_main")))` in
Canada** (mean |Δ| =
`r f2(pick(cors, mean_abs_change, dataset_label == dl("pilot_western_ca_main")))`
z there; the double-block runs drop, short runs rise). Validity barely moves
except in two datasets: Canada, where the rate is more valid, and Argentina,
where it is less valid because of its many short runs (section 2B).
Stability across waves is unchanged. So the switch is about **fairness of
individual scores**, especially for any longitudinal use of the Canadian
data, but the 30-s floor lets very short runs through.

**3. Efficiency modeling: a four-rung ladder, and the rate score holds up
best.** No model-based alternative beats it overall. The one that matches
it on validity (EZ drift) is much less stable, and the one that matches it
on stability in Germany and Bogotá (zero-fill) is less valid. The
scoreboard below compares all methods on every available metric.

## Scoreboard: every method × every metric

Validity columns are n-weighted means of within-dataset correlations
(criteria: the production PA/SWR/Vocab/TROG θ in `r data_ref`, each child's
first run per task). Reliability uses the best available estimator per
method: odd/even-trial split-half with Spearman–Brown for the
trial-computable scores (rate, EZ), model-based empirical reliability for
the latent-score methods (zero-fill: mirt EAP r~xx~; SA:
var(θ̂)/(var(θ̂)+mean(SE²))). Stability columns use each child's first two
runs at least six months apart, the same pairs for every method (runs
missing any method's score are dropped), in datasets with at least 20
pairs.

```{r scoreboard-methods}
# one frame of run-level scores for every method, z within dataset
methods_run <- scores_cmp |>
  select(dataset, run_id, rate = score_new) |>
  full_join(zf |> select(dataset, run_id, zerofill = zf_z),
            by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  full_join(sa_run |> select(dataset, run_id, sa_composite = eff),
            by = c("dataset", "run_id")) |>
  full_join(ez_run |> group_by(dataset) |>
              mutate(ez_drift = scale(drift)[, 1]) |> ungroup() |>
              select(dataset, run_id, ez_drift),
            by = c("dataset", "run_id"))
if (has_ddm) {
  methods_run <- methods_run |>
    full_join(ddm$run |> group_by(dataset) |>
                mutate(ddm_drift = scale(drift_re)[, 1]) |> ungroup() |>
                select(dataset, run_id, ddm_drift),
              by = c("dataset", "run_id"))
}
method_levels <- intersect(
  c("rate", "zerofill", "sa_composite", "ddm_drift", "ez_drift"),
  names(methods_run))

# criteria: age + other language/reading tasks (first run per child)
crit_wide <- registry_scores |>
  filter(task %in% c("pa", "swr", "vocab", "trog"), !is.na(ability)) |>
  left_join(run_data |> select(run_id, user_id, time_started), by = "run_id") |>
  left_join(participants |> select(user_id, dataset), by = "user_id") |>
  filter(!is.na(dataset)) |>
  first_run(task) |>
  select(dataset, user_id, task, crit_score = ability) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = task, values_from = crit_score)

board <- sre_scores_pub |>
  first_run() |>
  select(dataset, user_id, run_id, age) |>
  left_join(crit_wide, by = c("dataset", "user_id")) |>
  inner_join(methods_run, by = c("dataset", "run_id"))

validity <- board |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(method_levels), names_to = "method",
               values_to = "score") |>
  filter(!is.na(score)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(age, pa, swr, vocab, trog), names_to = "criterion",
               values_to = "crit") |>
  filter(!is.na(crit)) |>
  group_by(method, criterion, dataset) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(), r = cor(score, crit), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(method, criterion) |>
  summarise(r = weighted.mean(r, n), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = criterion, values_from = r) |>
  select(method, age, pa, swr, vocab, trog)
```

```{r scoreboard-reliability}
# split-half (odd/even trials, Spearman-Brown) for rate and EZ
halves <- sre |>
  mutate(half = ifelse(trial_number %% 2 == 0, "even", "odd")) |>
  group_by(dataset, run_id, half) |>
  summarise(rate_h = (sum(correct) - sum(!correct)) / sum(rt_s) * 180,
            n_h = n(), pc_h = mean(correct),
            mrt_h = mean(rt_s[correct & rt_s >= 0.25 & rt_s <= 30]),
            vrt_h = var(rt_s[correct & rt_s >= 0.25 & rt_s <= 30]),
            nc_h = sum(correct), .groups = "drop")

sb <- \(r) 2 * r / (1 + r)
wmean_by_ds <- \(df, x1, x2) df |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  filter(n() >= 20) |>
  summarise(n = n(), r = cor({{x1}}, {{x2}}, use = "complete.obs"),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(rel = sb(weighted.mean(r, n))) |> pull(rel)

rate_halves <- halves |>
  filter(n_h >= 5) |>
  select(dataset, run_id, half, rate_h) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = half, values_from = rate_h) |>
  filter(!is.na(odd), !is.na(even))
rel_rate <- wmean_by_ds(rate_halves, odd, even)

ez_halves <- halves |>
  filter(n_h >= 8, nc_h >= 5, !is.na(vrt_h), vrt_h > 0) |>
  mutate(pc_adj = pmin(pmax(pc_h, 0.5 + 1 / (2 * n_h)), 1 - 1 / (2 * n_h)),
         drift_h = ez_diffusion(pc_adj, vrt_h, mrt_h)$drift) |>
  select(dataset, run_id, half, drift_h) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = half, values_from = drift_h) |>
  filter(!is.na(odd), !is.na(even))
rel_ez <- wmean_by_ds(ez_halves, odd, even)

# model-based empirical reliability for the latent-score methods
rel_zf <- zf |> distinct(bank, rxx) |>
  left_join(zf |> count(bank), by = "bank") |>
  summarise(rel = weighted.mean(rxx, n)) |> pull(rel)

rel_sa <- sa_run |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarise(err = mean((theta_se / sd(theta))^2) + mean((tau_se / sd(tau))^2),
            tot = var(scale(theta)[, 1] + scale(tau)[, 1]),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(rel = weighted.mean(pmax(0, 1 - err / tot), n)) |> pull(rel)

rel_ddm <- if (has_ddm) ddm$run |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  summarise(rel = var(drift_re) / (var(drift_re) + mean(drift_se^2)),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(rel = weighted.mean(rel, n)) |> pull(rel) else NA_real_

reliability <- tibble(
  method = c("rate", "zerofill", "sa_composite", "ddm_drift", "ez_drift"),
  reliability = c(rel_rate, rel_zf, rel_sa, rel_ddm, rel_ez),
  rel_type = c("split-half (SB)", "EAP rxx", "model rxx", "model rxx",
               "split-half (SB)"))
```

```{r scoreboard-stability}
stab_all <- stability_by_dataset(methods_run, method_levels)

# one stability column per dataset, labelled with its pairs and median gap
stab_names <- with(stab_all, glue(
  "Stability: {dataset_label} ({round(gap_months)} mo, n = {n_pairs})"))

stability <- stab_all |>
  select(dataset_label, all_of(method_levels)) |>
  pivot_longer(-dataset_label, names_to = "method") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset_label, values_from = value,
              names_prefix = "stab_")
```

```{r scoreboard-table}
method_labels <- c(
  rate = "Rate (C − I per s; production)",
  zerofill = "Zero-filled Rasch (ROAR)",
  sa_composite = "Hierarchical SA composite",
  ddm_drift = "Diffusion-IRT drift",
  ez_drift = "EZ-diffusion drift")

scoreboard <- validity |>
  left_join(reliability, by = "method") |>
  left_join(stability, by = "method") |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = names(method_labels),
                         labels = method_labels)) |>
  arrange(method)

knitr::kable(scoreboard, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Method", "Age", "PA", "SWR", "Vocab", "TROG",
                           "Reliability", "(estimator)", stab_names),
             caption = "Scoring-method scoreboard. Validity = n-weighted mean within-dataset r; all scores z within dataset.")

# scoreboard values for the prose
sbv <- \(m, col) f2(pick(scoreboard, {{ col }}, method == method_labels[[m]]))
stab_col <- \(d) paste0("stab_", dl(d))
stab_range <- \(m) {
  x <- scoreboard |>
    filter(method == method_labels[[m]]) |>
    select(starts_with("stab_")) |>
    unlist()
  paste0(f2(min(x)), "–", f2(max(x)))
}
```

Reading the scoreboard:

- **The rate is the strongest primary score overall.** It is best on age
  (`r sbv("rate", "age")`), level with the best method on PA and SWR
  (`r sbv("rate", "pa")` and `r sbv("rate", "swr")`), and the most stable
  across waves in Bogotá and rural Colombia
  (`r sbv("rate", stab_col("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota"))` and
  `r sbv("rate", stab_col("pilot_uniandes_co_rural"))`). In Germany it ties
  zero-fill (`r sbv("rate", stab_col("pilot_mpieva_de_main"))` vs
  `r sbv("zerofill", stab_col("pilot_mpieva_de_main"))`). Its split-half
  reliability is `r sbv("rate", "reliability")`.
- **EZ drift tracks the language criteria as well as the rate, but is much
  less stable.** Its validity is PA `r sbv("ez_drift", "pa")`, SWR
  `r sbv("ez_drift", "swr")`, Vocab `r sbv("ez_drift", "vocab")` and TROG
  `r sbv("ez_drift", "trog")` (rate: `r sbv("rate", "pa")`,
  `r sbv("rate", "swr")`, `r sbv("rate", "vocab")`,
  `r sbv("rate", "trog")`). It is consistent within a session (split-half
  `r sbv("ez_drift", "reliability")`) but its stability across waves is only
  `r stab_range("ez_drift")`, against `r stab_range("rate")` for the rate.
- **The SA composite is below the rate on every validity criterion and on
  stability** (Vocab `r sbv("sa_composite", "vocab")` vs
  `r sbv("rate", "vocab")`; Germany stability
  `r sbv("sa_composite", stab_col("pilot_mpieva_de_main"))` vs
  `r sbv("rate", stab_col("pilot_mpieva_de_main"))`). The July version of
  this chapter read its speed dimension as buying validity on Vocab; that
  came from the criterion-join bug and doesn't hold.
- **Zero-fill has the highest model reliability
  (`r sbv("zerofill", "reliability")`) and ties the rate on stability in
  Germany and Bogotá, but it is less valid on every criterion** (PA
  `r sbv("zerofill", "pa")` vs `r sbv("rate", "pa")`, TROG
  `r sbv("zerofill", "trog")` vs `r sbv("rate", "trog")`), most of all where
  fast guessing is common (section 4). That fits a score that captures how
  much of the bank a fast, accurate reader reaches more than
  construct-general reading efficiency.

The diagnosis: SRE's net rate *is* the behaviorally meaningful quantity. It
bundles decision efficiency **and** stable individual differences in pacing
and caution, and the decompositions that strip the latter out (EZ and the SA
composite) lose stability. The site-dependent ability–speed correlation
(`r f2(min(sa_cor$r_theta_tau))` to `r f2(max(sa_cor$r_theta_tau))`,
section 4) also means no fixed recombination of decomposed parts travels
across sites. The diffusion-IRT comparison (item drift tracking item
accuracy and RT; person drift less stable than the rate) was established on
the retired hackathon data and hasn't been re-run here; see the callout
above.

**Recommendations for the DCC:**

- **Keep rate scoring.** Production has adopted it, with wall-clock span as
  the denominator (section 2). It fixes the Canadian double-block distortion
  at no modeling cost and is what the ROAR "net correct in 3 minutes" score
  means.
- **Flag or exclude very short runs.** The 30-s floor lets through runs that
  end long before the deadline. In Argentina
  `r round(100 * pick(short_share, share_short, dataset_label == dl("rfp1_utdt_ar_main")))`%
  of children's first runs are shorter than `r short_cut` s, and they pull
  the rate's validity below the legacy score's (section 2B). A higher floor
  or a run-level flag would fix this; first check what ends these runs.
- **If a measurement model is wanted**, the next step is an
  **offset-Poisson / Rasch-Poisson counts GLMM** (net-correct count with
  `offset(log(time))`, corpus fixed effects, child random effects). It is
  rate normalization with standard errors and corpus adjustment, not a new
  scoring philosophy.
- **Diffusion IRT: the July "don't use it" conclusion rests on the old data
  only.** The full hierarchical Wiener fit (9.5 h on Sherlock) was not
  re-run on `r data_ref`. What *is* re-confirmed here is the narrower claim
  that splitting the rate into separate ability and speed components
  (EZ-diffusion, the hierarchical SA model) loses stability across waves
  relative to the simple rate score. That is consistent with, but not proof
  of, the same conclusion for full diffusion IRT. The old fit remains in
  `data/sre_ddm_estimates.rds` for questions about the speed–accuracy
  tradeoff, not as a score.
- **Use RT for data quality regardless.** Sub-second responses are at
  chance in the Spanish-speaking sites and Ghana, where they make up
  `r with(filter(guess_tab, dataset_label %in% dataset_labels_named[c("pilot_uniandes_co_bogota", "pilot_uniandes_co_rural", "rfp1_utdt_ar_main", "pilot_capecoast_gh_main")]), paste0(round(100 * min(pct_rt_under_1s)), "–", round(100 * max(pct_rt_under_1s))))`%
  of trials. A fast-guess flag (e.g. the share of RT < 1 s) is a cheap,
  useful run-level QC covariate.
- **Look into Ghana's SRE data.** Accuracy is near chance even on slower
  responses, and scores are unrelated to age (section 3).

For reference, the patch this chapter proposed in July 2026. Production
adopted the same rate, with wall-clock span as the denominator:


```r
score_sre <- \(trial_data_task, dataset) {
  trial_data_task |>
    group_by(.data$run_id) |>
    summarise(elapsed = sum(.data$rt_numeric, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000,
              net = sum(.data$correct) - sum(!.data$correct)) |>
    filter(.data$elapsed >= 30) |>
    mutate(score = scale(.data$net / .data$elapsed * 180)[, 1],
           score_type = "guessing_adjusted_rate_scaled") |>
    select(-"elapsed", -"net")
}
```
